input_lifecycle.touch_began: create one pooled FXTouch only when active drag count is below 1; position; activate; play root ParticleSystem with children
input_lifecycle.touch_moved_or_stationary: clamp screen x/y to camera pixel bounds and move the active effect
input_lifecycle.touch_ended_or_canceled: remove the pointer mapping immediately, then recycle the effect after its Duration * 60 end-of-frame yields
input_lifecycle.mouse: same lifecycle using pointer id INT_MAX and the left mouse button

runtime_behavior.input_latency_note: No programmed trail delay exists. The active effect transform follows each Moved or Stationary sample; TrailRenderer adds geometry subject only to its minimum vertex distance and retains it for 0.3 seconds. The 60-frame release wait is pool recycling, not head lag.
runtime_behavior.recycle_note: This is frame-count based (WaitForEndOfFrame), not elapsed-time based.
recycle_sequence: clear TrailRenderer and stop root ParticleSystem with children

fx_touch_component.awake: cache root ParticleSystem and copy main.duration to Duration

trail_timescale_guard.below_or_equal_threshold: park existing TrailRenderer positions and progressively drain them; then clear and disable renderer
trail_timescale_guard.above_threshold: clear parked positions and re-enable renderer

viewport_reference.screen_ratio_rule: For an orthographic camera, CSS pixels per world unit = viewport_css_height / (2 * orthographic_size). At orthographic size 1, one world unit is half of viewport height; multiply again by devicePixelRatio only for physical canvas backing pixels.
viewport_reference.canvas_radius_note: Unity particle startSize is the full billboard dimension. If a Canvas renderer accepts radius, radius_css_px = startSize_world * viewport_css_height / (4 * orthographic_size). Trail width and minimum vertex distance are world lengths, so both use the full pixels-per-world-unit formula, not the radius formula.
